annotations.title: Feed my sheep.
annotations.text: As it was promised him Mat. 16. that the Church should be builded upon him, and that the keys of heaven should be given to him: so here it is performed, & he is actually made the general Pastor and Governor of all Christ's sheep. [1] For though the other ten (as Matthias and Paul also afterward) were Apostles, Bishops, Priests, and had authority to bind and loose, to remit and retain, to preach, baptise, and such like, as well as he: Yet in these things and all other government, Christ would have him to be their head, and they to depend of him as head of their College, and consequently of the whole flock of Christ: no Apostle nor no Prince in earth (if he acknowledge himself to be a sheep of Christ) exempted from his charge. And that Christ maketh a difference between Peter and the rest, and giveth him some greater preeminence and regiment than the rest, [2] it is plain by that he is asked whether he love our Lord more than the other Apostles also do. Where his special charge giveth no difference of love had been sufficient. To Peter (saith Cyprian) [3] our Lord after his Resurrection said, Feed my sheep, and builded his Church upon him alone, and to him he giveth the charge of feeding his sheep. For although after his Resurrection he gave his power alike to all, saying, As my Father sent me, so I send you, take the Holy Ghost, if you remit to any their sins, they shall be remitted &c. Yet to manifest unity, he constituted one Chair, & so disposed by his authority that unity should have origin of one. The rest of the Apostles were that Peter was, in equal fellowship of honour and power, but the beginning cometh of unity: the Primacy is given to Peter, that the Church of Christ may be shewed to be one Chair. S. Chrysostome also saith thus: [4] Why did our Lord shed his blood? truly to redeem those sheep, the care of which he committed both to Peter and also to his Successors. [5] And a little after, Christ would have Peter endued with such authority, and to be far above all his other Apostles: for he saith: Peter, dost thou love me more than all these do? Whereupon our Master might have inferred, If thou love me Peter, use much fasting, sleep on the hard flour, watch much, be patron to the oppressed, father to the orphans, and husband to the widows: but omitting all these things, he saith, Feed my sheep. For, all the foresaid virtues certainly be done easily of many subjects; but to bear the burden of the Principality, to undertake the government of the Church and committing the charge of so many souls, all woman kind must needs wholly give place to the burden and greatness thereof, and a great number of men also. So writeth he.

notes.text: Peter is here made the general Pastor, and the Church is builded upon him.
The Protestants otherwise denying this preeminence of Peter, yet to uphold their Archbishops, do avouch & prove it against the Puritanes.
Cypr. de unit. Ec. & li. 2. de Sacerd.
Peter's successors succeed him in universal authority.

annotations.title: Another shall gird thee.
annotations.text: He Prophesieth of Peter's Martyrdom, and of the kind of death which he should suffer, that was, crucifying.[1] Which [2] the Heretics fearing that it were a step to prove he was martyred in Rome, deny: whereas the Fathers and ancient writers are as plain in this, as that he was at Rome. Origen apud Euseb. li. 3. c. 1. Euseb. li. 2 c. 24. Hist. Ec. Tertul. de præscript. nu. 14. Aug. tract. 123 in Ioan. Chrysost. Bedæ in hunc locum.
